To: t-4471
Replying to: p01
Cc: none
Subject: Re: PSA: think twice about that "free" eviction clinic

Hi everyone — I'm Jasmine Holloway, a paralegal at Cascade Legal Rights Project. The moderator invited us to respond to this thread, and we want to.

First, I understand why people are upset. Getting a letter from a lawyer right after you ask for help with an eviction is scary, and it's fair to want to know where that letter came from. Nobody here is angry at anyone for raising it, and we're not going to argue with people by name.

Here's what our policy actually says. Landlords and their attorneys are prohibited recipients of anything from the clinic. Sharing, selling, or disclosing attendee information is a prohibited use, full stop. Sign-in sheets are kept internally in locked storage.

One thing that may explain the letters people are seeing: eviction filings are public records at the magistrate court, and some law firms pull those records and send solicitation mail to tenants. That's a likely explanation. We can't speak to any individual's situation, though, and we won't — out of respect for the people who came to us for help.

The clinic is still happening this Saturday, November 14. The library meeting room is closed that day, so we've moved to the fellowship hall at Mt Zion; the side entrance by the parking lot is accessible. Same time as always: 10am to 1pm, walk-in, no appointment needed.

If you have questions, email clinic@cascaderights.example or call the office at 404-555-0187 and we'll answer them.

If you're behind on rent, or you've got a court date coming up, you're still welcome. That hasn't changed.
